weeks.note: RECOVERY WEEK. Upper/Lower split: two upper sessions (Tue, Fri) so chest and back get 2x frequency at zero cost to running; one lower session (Thu), which is all the race can afford. Only two sessions actually matter: the talk test on a cool morning, and Saturday's descents.

sessions.label: UPPER A (push-emphasis) — bench/press + a row. No leg cost, won't touch tomorrow's test.
TALK TEST 5 km — MORNING, cool, fresh. Step the pace up every 3-5 min, say a sentence aloud, note the HR where it turns from comfortable to 'comfortable but harder'.
LOWER — own day, no running. Strength focus (squat/split squat, single-leg RDL, calf, tib, glute-med). NOT eccentric-emphasised — Saturday is the eccentric day.
Easy run 4 km (talk test) — or the TALK TEST if Wednesday slipped
UPPER B (pull-emphasis) — pull-ups/rows + a press. Second upper session: chest and back both hit 2x this week.
Vertical 25 min (stairs/ramp/incline) — climbing
Controlled stair/ramp descents after the vertical — THE eccentric session. First real descent load.

weeks.note: Barcelona Tue-Fri, then festival at Amsterdamse Bos (Fri evening, Sat, Sun). Down week — the travel timing is ideal; nothing here builds fitness. Benchmark deferred to a cool, recovered morning (Week 6). The long run folds into Sat festival morning. Festival walking covers the volume; do not add load.

sessions.label: Easy 3 km — Barcelona, early AM by feel. Heat inflates HR; ignore pace and HR, run by breath.
Optional vertical — hike Montjuic or Bunkers del Carmel in Barcelona. No benchmark this week; heat and travel would void the data.
Long run 6-7 km — Sat morning from Lelylaan into Amsterdamse Bos, easy by feel; scope the festival grounds. Hydrate hard before the day.

weeks.note: EASY RE-ENTRY — recovering from the festival weekend. No max efforts, no heavy legs, no CP test (moved to Week 6, now a power test on fresh legs). Optional easy 4 km Thu or rest — your call. Run easy by feel, hydrate; only if you feel decent. Getting back to baseline is the whole job this week.

sessions.label: Easy 4-5 km recovery jog — by feel, conversational, ignore pace/HR. Walk it in if you feel rough.
Easy 5-6 km by feel. Optional light pull if you are feeling good.
Easy bike ride instead of the long run — zero impact, aerobic recovery. Keep it chill; save the legs for Tuesday's power test.

weeks.note: First real fitness read of the block — the CP power test, Tuesday on fresh legs (Mon rest before it). Power, not HR: after the sensor audit, power is the channel we trust. This sets your real training zones. HR benchmark is shelved until a chest strap.

CP 3+12 power test — warm up, 12 min all-out even pace, 20-30 min easy, then 3 min all-out. Sets real power zones on fresh legs. Power is our trusted channel now.
Push (upper) — after the run, no leg cost

Easy run 6 km (talk test)
Pull (upper) — after the run
Long day 2h15 time-on-feet (run/walk, walk the climbs)

weeks.note: RESET WEEK. Two corrections that change everything. (1) You have steep terrain 20-25 MINUTES away - Zuid-Kennemerland dunes by train, faces at 30-45%. I told you the nearest hills were 2.5-3 h; that was wrong. (2) Your plan's vertical is an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE short: 40 min/week is ~400 m against a 2,003 m race. From here everything is measured in time and vertical metres, never kilometres. LOCKED WEEK SHAPE: Sun optional easy ride - MON REST - TUE legs + preconditioning walk ONLY (this is THE eccentric day - keep it focused, no upper) - WED easy run + strides + push - THU vertical + pull - FRI REST - SAT LONG DAY. Eccentric work sits 48 h apart throughout: Tue heavy, Thu moderate, Sat long. That spacing is the constraint - force loss needs 3 days to recover and soreness 4, so 24 h between eccentric sessions compounds damage instead of building tolerance. Cutbacks weeks 10 and 13. CUT ORDER: (1) Sunday ride, (2) Thursday vertical. Never Saturday's long day or Tuesday's legs. HYROX SEEDING STARTS: only via substitution inside Thursday's pull session - erg warm-up, farmers carry, dead hangs. NOT wall balls, sandbag lunges or burpee broad jumps - those are all quad and eccentric load competing directly with the descent block. NOT compromised running - it breaks the 80/20 distribution Madeira needs. The point is to arrive in November with technique and grip already built, so the first two Hyrox weeks are productive instead of remedial.

sessions.label: OPTIONAL easy ride 60-75 min - the day after the long day. Zero impact. THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO CUT when work bites.
Easy run 6 km (talk test) + 6-8 x 20 s strides after (relaxed, full recovery, not a workout)
Push (upper) - after the easy run. Fresh, not on legs you just destroyed.

Legs ONLY, no upper - heavy eccentric. Three quad lifts doing three different jobs: HEAVY BILATERAL trap-bar deadlift 4 x 4-6 at 85 kg (18 Aug: 75x6x3 with 4+ reps in reserve, so 1RM is nearer 100 - autoregulate to 2 REPS IN RESERVE and add 5 kg when the last set still feels easy), LOADED UNILATERAL Bulgarian split squat 3 x 8/leg with dumbbells, and TEMPO ECCENTRIC step-downs 3 x 8-10/leg with 3-4 s lowering. Then Nordics 3 x 5 and single-leg calf raises. Never to failure. 48-72 h before the long day. On a -15% descent hip drop is 23.7 mm vs 7.6 mm uphill (very large effect), so descending is a frontal-plane hip problem and not only a quad problem - loaded Bulgarians carry that demand, which is why standalone side planks and cable abduction came out. HYROX SLED TECHNIQUE at the end, 8-10 x 12.5 m at 50-65% load (~100 kg), 60-90 s rest. TECHNIQUE ONLY, never to fatigue. Forearms hooked on the posts, 30-45 deg lean, short choppy steps 20-30 cm at 3-4 per second, and never let the sled stop. Sled push is PURELY CONCENTRIC, so it costs your descent block nothing - which is why it is the one Hyrox station you can train now. At 56 kg you need 1.03x bodyweight of horizontal force to break a stationary sled versus 0.81x to keep one rolling, so learning not to stop is worth more to you than to anyone heavier. About 8 minutes.

VERTICAL 45 min - STAIRWELL, your own building or a car park. ~12 x 15 floors, about 540 m. Lift up, WALK DOWN - the descent is the point. Dutch stair pitch is 30-33 deg, inside the optimal climbing range, and Madeira is full of stone staircases. Zero travel, weather-proof.

Pull (upper) - after the vertical session. HYROX SEEDING, all substitutions not additions: (1) WARM UP ON THE SKIERG OR ROWER, 5-8 min, technique only - hinge and drive the first third of the pull, that is where 80% of ski power comes from. Replaces your normal warm-up, costs nothing. (2) SWAP one row variation for a HEAVY FARMERS CARRY, 4 x 40-60 m. Same pulling pattern, direct Hyrox transfer. (3) Finish with DEAD HANGS, 3 x max. Baseline 20 Aug was 32/36/31 s, so 90 s by October was never realistic: target 55-60 s by 1 Nov and 90 s by Hyrox in January. Grip takes 4-6 weeks to change and it is what limits the farmers carry. About 3 minutes total added to the session.
LONG DAY 1:50 time-on-feet, 300 m vert. Dunes if you can get there.

PRECONDITIONING DOWNHILL WALK - 5 minutes, 5.6 kg in the pack, walking DOWN stairs. Lift up, walk down, repeat for 5 min. ~110 m of descent, about 37 flights. One bout cuts strength loss 49%, CK 47%, soreness 66% a week later. Five minutes, in your own building, no travel.

weeks.note: Poles introduced this week. They save little metabolically but cut RPE 14-18% and measurably reduce muscle damage over a climb-and-descent day. Length = height x 0.67 = 107 cm, so 105 cm is the correct fit (Mountain King chart: 155-165 cm -> 105 cm). Nobody manufactures 93 cm - 100 cm is the shortest size made. Decathlon only sells 110/120/130, and its own chart puts 155-171 cm on 110, which is also what sub-165 cm coaches actually run. Buy the Kiprun 500 aluminium at 110 cm, EUR 70. Aluminium bends where carbon snaps, which is the right failure mode on wet basalt for a first-time pole user. Ultra X's 2026 race rules contain no restriction on poles.

LONG DAY 2:05, 500 m vert. First session with poles.

NEW SPEED SLOT - easy 5 km with the LAST 1 KM at threshold effort. Comfortably hard, three or four words at a time, HR 168-176 (max HR is 200, measured 7 Jun, not the 190 an age formula assumes). One kilometre, that is all. This is a progression run, not an interval session: you get a real quality stimulus for almost no recovery cost, in a week where vertical also goes 45 to 55 min and the long day goes 1:50 to 2:05. Volume is the thing being added this week - the last km is a taste, not the point.

weeks.note: GUT TRAINING STARTS. Target 60-80 g carb/h by week 14, from 40-50 now, +10 g every two weeks. No drop bags and no crew at Madeira - only ~2 checkpoints, ~10 km apart - so you carry 400-500 g of carbohydrate yourself. Rehearse the weight and the stowage, not just the products. INTENSITY STARTS THIS WEEK, on flat ground: Thursday's vertical stays STEADY because Hyrox is 8 x 1 km flat and stair fitness does not transfer. Target distribution is 80-85% easy, 15-20% hard. ORDER CHANGED 31 Aug - threshold Mon -> Tue, legs Tue -> Wed, easy run + push Wed -> Mon. Reason is measurement, not fatigue: resting HR was 55 against a 50-52 baseline and HRV 78 against an 89 weekly average, which distorts the HR-work relationship in both directions. This is the first structured interval session of the block and its job is to establish what threshold feels like - a reference set on a distorted day gets trained off for weeks. Load is unchanged: three runs, two gym sessions, one vertical, one rest day, Friday still free. Legs on Wednesday keeps 72 h before the long day, the outer edge of the 48-72 h rule. Push stays paired with the easy run, pull with the vertical. STOPPING RULE: the threshold session happens Tuesday regardless of readiness unless sleep is under 6 h or HRV drops below 70.

KIT REHEARSAL: load the vest to ~2.6 kg with full race carbohydrate (~13 gels plus pre-measured mix) and walk 60 min. Checkpoints are WATER ONLY - you carry every calorie across three ~2h10 legs. Drink mix must stay 6-8%: a 500 ml flask holding 80 g is 16%, and 42% of a 10% drink is still in the stomach an hour later.

PRECONDITIONING DOWNHILL WALK - 5 minutes, 5.6 kg in the pack, walking DOWN stairs. Lift up, walk down, repeat for 5 min. ~110 m of descent, about 37 flights. One bout cuts strength loss 49%, CK 47%, soreness 66% a week later. Five minutes, in your own building, no travel.

THRESHOLD 4 x 4 min, 90 s easy jog between. Warm up 10 min, cool down 10 min. Comfortably hard - three or four words at a time, HR 168-176 (max HR 200, measured - your easy runs already sit at 161, so 160-168 would not be a stimulus). Your first structured interval session: threshold before VO2max because it recovers faster and you are two weeks into having a third run at all.

weeks.note: Cutback. Deliberate, and the reason matters: in trail runners, injury weeks were preceded by load DROPPING 16-24% then rebounding 15-37%. Yo-yo loading, not absolute load, is what precedes injury. This dip is planned and the rebound is controlled. RESHUFFLED 6 Sep: time trial held on Monday (Sunday is a full rest day, which is the setup a TT wants - 9.6 h sleep and HRV 98 the night before), pull moved to Tuesday as the recovery day, legs to Wednesday, easy 5 km to Friday, and Thursday's stairwell session replaced by casual football. Three runs held: TT, Friday easy, Saturday long. Push moved Wednesday -> Tuesday: Tuesday is now a single upper day and Wednesday is legs only.

Push (upper) - TUESDAY, paired with pull as a single UPPER DAY. Legs do nothing either way, so it doubles as the time-trial recovery day and it leaves Wednesday as a short, focused legs session 24 h before football. Upper/lower beats push/pull/legs on real-world adherence and the strength difference is 3-4% once adherence is controlled, which is noise - the split that actually gets done wins.

LONG DAY 2:00, 600 m vert - upgraded from 1:30/400 m. This is the bridge in the vertical ladder: 600 m here keeps week 11's 800 m at +33% rather than a jump off 400 m. It is also five times your best long-day vertical ever (118 m), so the vertical is the session - the kilometres are incidental. Expect legs 36 h off an hour of football, so start conservatively and let the vertical, not the pace, be the target. Floor is 500 m if Friday feels rough.

5 KM TIME TRIAL - the number this whole plan has been missing. Warm up 10-15 min easy + 4-6 x 20 s strides + 3-4 min rest. Then 5 km flat, hard as you can SUSTAIN. Go out at 5:15/km and hold, check in at 2 km, kick from 4 km. Do NOT start at 4:40 - a blown TT gives an unusable number. Flat, no lights, no turns: Vondelpark outer loop or the Amstel. Auto-lap every 1 km. Down week with Sunday rest behind you.

FOOTBALL 21:00 - casual 8-a-side, 1 hour. This REPLACES the 40 min stairwell session; do not do both. The vertical that builds toward Madeira is the long day's, not this one, and cutting it in a down week does not touch the Saturday-to-Saturday ladder. Warm up properly before kick-off - the cutting and decelerating is the highest acute injury risk in your week and an ankle ends the race. Finish 22:00, eat, bed by midnight: Saturday's long day is 36 h later, right through the DOMS peak.

weeks.note: TERRAIN WEEKEND #1 of 2 - Posbank/Veluwezoom, ~1h15 by car, ~EUR 30 of petrol. Hard-surface descents, 90-110 m climbs. Twenty reps is 1,800 m of real ascent AND descent. One day there beats ten stairwell sessions, because sand is compliant and actually REDUCES muscle damage relative to firm ground. Madeira is rock and stone steps. REVISED 6 Sep: this was the highest-risk week in the plan - VO2max, heavy eccentric legs, 70 min of stairs and a 2:35/900 m long day, all landing off a 14.9 km week. Thursday's stairs cut 70 -> 50 min and the long day 900 -> 800 m, taking weekly vertical from 1,740 m to ~1,300 m. Running kilometres are unchanged at 33: that equals a week already completed on 24 August, and percentage progression rules mislead at 20-35 km/wk where a 10% step is 2 km.

TIME IS THE PRESCRIPTION and vertical is only the check: finishing near 400 m is fine, do not chase the number by rushing the climbs. LONG DAY 2:30, 800 m vert - trimmed from 2:35/900 m. Your best long-day vertical ever is 118 m, so week 10's 600 m is already a five-fold jump; 800 m here keeps the ladder at 600 -> 800 -> 1,100 instead of a 50% step onto ground you have never covered - Posbank if possible, descents on hard surface DESCENT CUE: shorten the step, 185-195 spm. Understriding cut strength loss to -8.8% vs -15.5% at preferred step length - roughly halved. Do NOT coach foot strike: the more anterior the strike, the LARGER the quad torque loss. Let the terrain dictate it.

VO2MAX 5 x 3 min HARD, 2 min easy jog. Warm up 10 min, cool down 10 min. Harder than threshold - one word at a time, HR 180-190. Pace off the week 10 TT: roughly your 5 km pace, no faster. THIS IS NOW YOUR ONLY HARD SESSION, so run it properly. It is the single session that most moves 5 km pace, and 5 km pace is what your Hyrox runs are made of.

weeks.note: Biggest vertical week so far, ~2,000-2,300 m. HR is now unreliable as a guide: in mountain ultras heart rate FALLS ~34 bpm across the race while RPE rises from 4.3 to 6.9. Pace off knee-extensor RPE - how your quads feel - not the watch.

About 8 minutes.

VERTICAL 75 min STEADY - stairwell, your own building or a car park. WALK UP, LIFT DOWN. Wet volcanic rock and wet wooden steps sit at friction 0.3-0.5 - barely enough to stand on a 28% slope, let alone brake. In the wet, zig-zagging and side-stepping are technique, not cowardice.

weeks.note: RACE WEEK. Sunday 1 Nov, Calhau de Sao Jorge to Machico. THE START IS 11:00, NOT DAWN - sunset is 18:17 and civil twilight ends 18:41. A 6:30 finish is daylight; 7:00 is dusk; 7:30 is DARK on exposed cliff paths. YOUR HEADTORCH IS SAFETY KIT, NOT A FORMALITY - carry it charged. The late start also gives you an unhurried fuelling morning: eat properly, this is an advantage. CHECKPOINTS ARE WATER ONLY - the 'water and snacks' line is wrong. Carry 420-490 g of carbohydrate yourself (~13 gels plus mix) across three ~2h10 legs, roughly 2.6 kg of vest. Only ~2 checkpoints, ~10 km apart. KIT: 1.5 L hydration capacity, taped-seam hooded waterproof, emergency blanket, 800 kcal reserve, phone with GPX, spare warm layer, and a BEAKER of at least 15 cl - bottles and flasks are explicitly not accepted. Checks are enforced. CALIBRATION from the 2025 field (n=34): winner 3:02:21, median 5:24:37 (13.0 min/km), last finisher 8:03:43, cut-off 11.5 h. Your target is 6:15-6:45. The 25K is the final 25 km of the 50K route - the organiser gave the SHORT race the STEEPEST ground, 80 m/km against 63.5 for the 50K. PACING - the single strongest result in the literature (n=23,207): in 91% of races, slower finishers overspent in the FIRST segment; after the opening everyone paces the rest alike. The damage is done at the start. Hike every gradient above 15% from the gun. HR: race average 138-150, climb ceiling 155, descents 120-140. Above 160 for two minutes on a climb, walk. Your 17 km run averaged 163 - you cannot hold that for six hours. THE DESCENT IS THE RACE. Racing the first steep descent saves ~10 minutes and costs 17-46 minutes later: 3:1 to 5:1 against, before you count the fall risk. And it will never feel hard - VO2 on descents is only 79% of threshold versus 100% uphill, so your breathing will tell you nothing. That is the trap. Short steps, 185-195 spm, gaze 4-5 m ahead on the second upcoming foothold, walk the stone staircases, zig-zag the wet sections. IN-RACE DIAGNOSTIC: compare climb rate per heartbeat on the second climb against the first. More than 5% worse means you overcooked the descent - concede ten minutes immediately and save the day. FUEL: 60-75 g/h at 2:1 glucose:fructose, drink to thirst, skip the salt capsules (no evidence they prevent hyponatraemia or cramp). Carb load 8-10 g/kg for 36-48 h = 450-560 g. Caffeine ~100 mg at 3 h and 75-100 mg at 4.5 h, 150-200 mg total - do not scale from 70 kg examples. WEATHER: use Santana on the north coast, not Funchal - 18 C max, 110 mm of rain across ~40% of days. Wet basalt and hypothermia are the risks here, not heat. Bib pickup Fri 30 Oct or Sat 31 Oct, 18:00-20:00, Machico Forum. No crew, no pacers, no drop bags.
